`~/.claude/skills/sitrep` is a prose specification of dira's query surface, executed by
an LLM re-reading markdown each time instead of by a query engine over structured
entries. Its ledger mode maps onto the entry model almost one-to-one — decisions with
provenance, parks *with their revival trigger*, reversals, routed open questions,
not-yet-planned work, and merged-versus-verified — and it states dira's own purpose
independently: that a fresh session cannot tell a ratified decision from a plausible
suggestion an agent made once, so it re-argues settled things or builds on unagreed
ones.

Two of its rules exist **only** because the data is unstructured, and dissolve rather
than transfer: the no-bare-IDs rule is an artifact of ids living in one file and their
descriptions in another, and "never from memory alone, verify anything surprising" is
`dec-0004`'s derived-never-stored done by hand.

## Four invariants this makes explicit

The design assumed these; the skill proves they are load-bearing. Each is checkable.

1. **No bare refs in output.** Any ref emitted by `brief`, `map`, `why`, or `check`
   carries its title in the same breath. A reader who has never opened the ledger must
   understand every line without looking anything up.
2. **Provenance is displayed, not merely stored.** On any surface a human disposes
   from, a human-confirmed decision must be visually distinguishable from an
   agent-staged guess. `source.tier` and `confirmed_by` exist in the schema; nothing
   said they must render, and an unrendered provenance field is the exact failure the
   skill's "never report a subagent's claim as fact" rule guards against.
3. **A deferral with no revival trigger is reported as a defect.** The skill's phrasing
   is the correct one: *a park without a trigger is not a decision, it is forgetting
   with better vocabulary.* This is the open gap where nine recorded `revisit_if`
   conditions sit inert with nothing watching them — the skill independently identifies
   the same defect class, which is what promotes it from a nice-to-have to a
   requirement.
4. **Contradictions are surfaced, never silently resolved.** Where two records
   conflict, both are named and neither is quietly preferred. This is `dira check`, and
   it extends to `map` and `brief`: a derived view that hides a conflict to look tidy
   is worse than one that reports it.

## The boundary — what dira must never take

dira derives the **states**. The human keeps the **verdict**: the trajectory sentence,
the weighted percentage, the risk list, the trend against the last report. Those are
synthesis, and taking them would need a narrative field that `cst-0002` forbids for
good reason — a compass reports a bearing, it does not tell you how the voyage is
going.

So the replacement is not "dira prints the sitrep." It is: `/sitrep` shrinks to a thin
judgement layer over `dira map` plus `gh`, and stops re-deriving state by hand.

## Why this is the first replacement target

`int-0003` has been the vaguest intent in the ledger — "at least two tools are
uninstalled and not missed" names no tool and no date, so nothing could falsify it.
`/sitrep` is a concrete, daily-used, self-owned surface whose manual labour is exactly
what dira automates, and whose correctness is verifiable against reports already
written. It is the honest first dogfood: if dira cannot reduce this skill, the
tool-reduction thesis is weaker than claimed.

The measurable form: the skill's gather phase currently reads `docs/plan.md`,
`docs/roadmap.md`, `gh pr list`, claim refs and prior reports, then hand-glosses every
id. When `dira map` supplies the four states with titles and provenance attached, that
phase reduces to two calls — and the report that produced this entry, written entirely
by hand, becomes the before-measurement.
